correctness.rationale: For each n≥3 and 2≤m<n, rank exchangeability gives J=j mass m/[j(j−1)] or censoring mass m/n, and conditional suffix ranks are uniform, proving the exact marked unsigned-Stirling law. A monotone record-exposure identity and harmonic sum prove the marginal checks. Exponential transformation of suffix record values yields a unit-rate Poisson process with threshold equal in law to the maximum of m exponentials, deriving the product of independent zero-based geometrics. The finite/infinite coupling fails only when the prefix maximum persists through n, probability m/n. Lyapunov applies to the independent geometric sum for m=o(n); for m/n→α∈(0,1), uniform conditional CLT away from blocks of length o(n) plus tail m/j gives independence of Gaussian count and censored Pareto mark. The script exhaustively checks all permutations through n=8, not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: The checked primary papers and public research record give classical uniform-record Stirling counts, record-value transforms and an exact m=1 one-arrival law, all fully credited. Their statements do not imply the new exact joint count/first-recovery law for deletion batches m≥2 or the independent Gaussian–censored-Pareto joint limit without additional conditioning and asymptotic proof. Multiple alias and broader-coverage searches were executed; absolute priority is uncertain because older general record-process coverage could be indexed differently.
residual_risks: General time-reversal/record-process identities not indexed as prefix deletion may independently yield the marked batch theorem.
Older record-process survey theorems may cover finite mixtures or infinite geometric factorization under a different name.

value.rationale: Batch erasure of early observations is a natural perturbation to an online running-maximum record monitor: false retroactive upper records are exposed until the previous threshold is first recovered. The joint law quantifies count, recovery clock and nonrecovery probability, rather than only an already-known one-arrival marginal. A finite-to-macroscopic transition yields an unexpected censored Pareto clock independent of Gaussian false-record fluctuations, with direct mathematical use in restarting/thinning record monitoring; this structural coupling is not merely the harmonic expectation or a renamed Stirling coefficient.
